title: fix: allow trusted scheduled Discord channel edits
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Trusted operator-created scheduled jobs have no inbound Discord sender. Before this change, `channel-edit` failed at the channel administration check even when the job had valid `message` access. Related: #140978.

This PR carries the canonical job grant through Discord channel editing, channel-name resolution, and provider retries. It uses the scheduled message admission and current tool-policy evaluation landed in #150166. It also fixes a caller completion check that discarded an accepted edit when disabling the job canceled its generated MCP request.

## User Impact

Operator-created jobs with `message` access can edit Discord channels and use the action's existing thread edit options. Configured account and action restrictions, the job's current capability, and Discord permissions continue to apply.

Disabling, removing, replacing, or narrowing a job blocks later requests and rate-limit retries. Caller or plugin retirement also blocks subsequent I/O. Configuration changes apply to the next invocation; an admitted operation retains its configuration. A confirmed provider result survives job cancellation and the original MCP request's abort.

## Why This Change Was Made

The optional SDK field `ChannelMessageActionAdapter.writeAuthorityActions?: readonly ChannelMessageActionName[]` declares that an adapter preserves the existing `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` callback through preparation and every provider request or retry. Action discovery and read support do not establish that write contract. The host independently selects eligible actions; Discord declares only `channel-edit` in this PR.

Admission checks the canonical job grant, configured action and account, and the active bundled or loader-verified official registration. Channel lookup retains the selected registration and request guard. Its read scope closes before the mutation, whose actual result is allowed to settle. The in-process Gateway retains the original signal and caller guards for later dispatches and mutation commits.

Older adapters remain source-compatible because the declaration is optional. Scheduled administration requires the updated adapter contract and its loaded registration. Account-created jobs do not inherit operator administration, and no run-wide owner flag or invented requester identity is introduced. Canonical SDK and automation documentation explains the interface, retained checks, configuration timing, and upgrade behavior.

## Evidence

The existing isolated fixture exercises the real scheduler, CLI child protocol or embedded runner, generated HTTP MCP grants, registered Gateway handler, and official Discord adapter. Only model decisions and provider responses are synthetic. The original scheduler failure submitted no PATCH. A separate regression reproduced channel-directory I/O after revocation; the repaired path blocks it.

All six scheduler scenarios passed: the two read controls, CLI and embedded edits, disable-before-429-retry, and accepted-response settlement after the original MCP signal aborts. The disable cases use real `cron.update` calls, inspect the persisted disabled job, and verify the exact authenticated PATCH and completed run cleanup.

The operator-only candidate passed 477 selected runtime tests, core/root typing, all 20 selected core test type graphs, formatting, targeted lint, source ratchets, and both import-cycle checks. Retained proof covers outbound/registry/Discord siblings and SDK declaration compatibility. Independent implementation, caller-settlement, and integration reviews found no actionable issues; the recorded default-P0 automated reviews are clean.

The three writer commits were replayed unchanged onto main after #150166 landed. Final head `4c1df7ac6bbd36aac84cf376e7052168f0b2cde4` preserves all 20 contribution files from the tested current-main integration candidate `e95ace9ce0841849a2e29f87bad86fe49bbd98cb` (tree `1578b5592e5bb2e943393d450acc369415d7122b`). That run includes the prerequisite's run-lifetime correction, the updated MCP request scope and CLI watchdog, and a controlled 120-second clock gap before CLI tool discovery. All six scheduler scenarios and combined core/root typing passed. Later main changes were checked against the writer's contracts; the recorded integration review is clean. The [current-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/35176003186) is Platinum with no code or security findings. [Current CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35175801747) has one unrelated Qwen timeout-equality failure and its aggregate: the test expected `120000` after one elapsed millisecond, receiving `119999`; 1,295 other cases in that bundle passed. The matching main-branch baseline failures are recorded in #150523, whose repair has landed in main. Those reported baseline runs used macOS/Node 26.8.2; this CI failure used Linux/Node 24.19.0. Source comparison tied the CI failure to the baseline's unchanged timeout/test inputs, with no writer interaction; the final main result retains the repair.

The scheduler and retained MCP cases checked these outcomes against the Gateway and fixture HTTP peers:

| Scenario | Checked provider and tool outcome |
|---|---|
| Account or forged-sender job | The three account-administration calls are rejected with no PATCH; the named-target case issues no provider request. |
| Operator edit, CLI and embedded | One authenticated `PATCH /api/v10/channels/100000000000000003`; the returned channel contains the requested topic. |
| Job disabled before a 429 response | The stored job is disabled; one PATCH only, no retry; the MCP result is an error; active Cron runs drain to zero. |
| Job disabled before an accepted 200 response | The original MCP signal aborts before the response is released; one PATCH only; `isError` is false and the returned channel/topic is preserved; active Cron runs drain to zero. |

Current-head assertions: [durable disablement and original-signal abort](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4c1df7ac6bbd36aac84cf376e7052168f0b2cde4/test/cron-message-read.integration.test.ts#L617), [tool outcome and sole PATCH](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4c1df7ac6bbd36aac84cf376e7052168f0b2cde4/test/cron-message-read.integration.test.ts#L681), and [account/forged-sender denial](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4c1df7ac6bbd36aac84cf376e7052168f0b2cde4/test/cli-message-authority.integration.test.ts#L791).

The account-denial and additional lifetime cases ran on the writer patch before the parent move. That verified tree was subsequently committed as `2128bd6`. Nineteen contribution files remain byte-identical; the shared scheduler fixture gained the prerequisite's clock-gap setup, exercised by the current-main run above.
